description: Evaluates the CodeTerm General Agent system prompt for correct behavioral responses

evals.name: implicit-request-ask-not-act
evals.prompt: [Telegram: 123456789] как там мой проект на workstation, все ок?
evals.expected_output: Agent queries the workstation peer (either actively via send-text or passively via get-output), NOT create workspaces or spawn agents
expectations: Queries the workstation peer via mesh — either actively (`send-text --pane general --mesh workstation`) or passively (`get-output --pane general --mesh workstation`, `pane list --mesh workstation`). Any of these counts.
Does NOT use workspace create
Does NOT use agent spawn
Eventually replies back to the Telegram user with bridge send (may happen after receiving info from workstation, or as a placeholder 'checking now, will report back')

evals.name: explicit-request-create-workspace
evals.prompt: [Telegram: 123456789] открой Example Project из ~/Developer/example-project и заспавнь агента чтоб разобрался
evals.expected_output: Agent creates workspace at project root and spawns an agent there
expectations: Uses workspace create with project name
Uses agent spawn with --task and --workspace
Creates ONE workspace at ~/Developer/example-project root, not per sub-folder

evals.name: mesh-spawn-orchestrator-not-worker
evals.prompt: [Telegram: 123456789] запусти билд и тесты на workstation в ~/Developer/myapp
evals.expected_output: Agent spawns orchestrator on the remote machine (any peer name resolving to 'workstation'), not a worker or lead
expectations: Uses `codeterm agent spawn` with a `--mesh <peer>` flag (any peer name — the exact name may be translated via memory/aliases)
Uses --role Orchestrator (explicit) or has no --role flag (spawn defaults to Orchestrator)
Does NOT use --role Worker or --role Lead
Does NOT inject --parent with a local pane ID

evals.name: recon-before-action
evals.prompt: [Telegram: 123456789] глянь что за проект ~/Developer/something-new, разберись что там
evals.expected_output: Agent explores the directory first (raw bash in its own pane OR via pane exec / send-text to another pane), not immediately creating a workspace
expectations: Explores the directory first — any of `ls`, `cat README`, `git log`, `tree`, or equivalent — before any `codeterm workspace create`
Does NOT immediately call `codeterm workspace create` without looking
Exploration may be raw bash in the agent's own shell (ls/cat/git) OR `codeterm pane exec` / `codeterm send-text` to delegate to another pane — BOTH are valid approaches

evals.name: telegram-photo-response
evals.prompt: [Telegram: 123456789] скинь мне вчерашние логи билда как файл
evals.expected_output: Agent sends the log file via bridge send --type document (or photo for images), not as terminal text
expectations: Uses `bridge send --to 123456789` with either `--type document` or `--type photo` and a `--file` flag pointing to an actual file path
Does NOT paste the raw log content as Telegram message text
Does NOT use base64 or binary data inline

evals.name: mesh-prefix-correct-reply
evals.prompt: [Mesh: workstation pane=a3f1b2c7] hey can you check disk usage and let me know?
evals.expected_output: Agent checks disk, replies to the EXACT pane on the EXACT peer
expectations: Replies via send-text --pane a3f1b2c7 --mesh workstation
Does NOT reply to --pane general
Does NOT use bridge send (that's for Telegram)

evals.name: mixed-prefixes-routing
evals.prompt:
[Telegram: 123456789] статус
[Mesh: home-server pane=deadbeef] need CPU info
evals.expected_output: Agent routes each message to correct channel
expectations: Telegram reply uses bridge send --to 123456789
Mesh reply uses send-text --pane deadbeef --mesh home-server
Does NOT mix up channels

evals.name: isolation-notes-storage
evals.prompt: запомни что юзер предпочитает dark theme и всегда хочет HTML formatting
evals.expected_output: Agent saves the preference via `codeterm mem save --kind preference ...` — mem is the source of truth, NOT MEMORY.md alone, NOT CLAUDE.md, NOT ~/.claude/
expectations: Uses `codeterm mem save` with `--kind preference` (the durable user preference kind) to persist the dark-theme + HTML-formatting preference
Does NOT rely solely on editing `MEMORY.md` via Write/Edit — mem is the source of truth; MEMORY.md alone is legacy and won't survive
Does NOT write to CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, or AGENT.md (those are auto-generated and forbidden)
Does NOT write to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, ~/.claude/projects/<...>/memory/, ~/.claude/settings, or any global/provider Claude config

evals.name: isolation-spawn-no-leak
evals.prompt: [Telegram: 123456789] открой проект ~/Developer/webapp и пусть агент пофиксит баг с логином
evals.expected_output: Agent spawns with task about the bug, NOT with General Agent prompt contents
expectations: Task in --task describes the bug fix, not General Agent instructions
Does NOT include Telegram routing or mesh instructions in --task
Does NOT paste or summarize the system prompt into the task

evals.name: telegram-streaming-append
evals.prompt: [Telegram: 123456789] объясни что такое mesh networking в CodeTerm
evals.expected_output: Agent uses send then --append for multi-part answer
expectations: First message uses bridge send (without --append)
Subsequent parts use --append flag
Uses HTML formatting tags

evals.name: workspace-tidiness
evals.prompt: [Telegram: 123456789] проверь что package.json в ~/Developer/myapp правильный
evals.expected_output: For a quick check, agent uses existing workspace or General workspace, NOT creating a new one
expectations: Does NOT create a new workspace for a simple file check
Uses cat/read or terminal command to check the file
May use pane exec or just run the command directly

evals.name: mono-repo-single-workspace
evals.prompt: [Telegram: 123456789] открой MyApp из ~/Developer/MyApp — там есть backend, frontend и ios подпроекты
evals.expected_output: Creates ONE workspace at ~/Developer/MyApp root, not separate workspaces per sub-project
expectations: Creates exactly ONE workspace
Workspace points to ~/Developer/MyApp root
Does NOT create separate workspaces for backend/frontend/ios
Agent inside will figure out sub-structure

evals.name: search-before-asking-skills
evals.prompt: какие у меня есть скиллы для работы с ffmpeg?
evals.expected_output: Agent runs `codeterm mem search --kind skill ffmpeg` (or equivalent mem query) before answering — mem is source of truth for skills
expectations: Uses `codeterm mem search` with `--kind skill` (and a query like `ffmpeg`) as the FIRST action before answering
Does NOT enumerate skills from the system prompt or memory without searching mem
Does NOT ask the user to list their own skills
Does NOT grep `~/.claude/skills/` or `~/.agents/skills/` on the filesystem — skills live in mem, not as files

evals.name: save-identity-to-mem
evals.prompt: зови меня Андрей с этого момента, я сеньор iOS разработчик
evals.expected_output: Agent saves identity via `codeterm mem save --kind preference --title identity ...` — identity is a mem_item, not a MEMORY.md edit
expectations: Uses `codeterm mem save` with `--kind preference` (and ideally `--title identity` or similar) to persist the name 'Андрей' and the senior iOS dev role
Does NOT write to `~/.claude/projects/<...>/memory/*.md` or any provider auto-memory path
Does NOT rely solely on editing `MEMORY.md` via Write/Edit — mem is the source of truth for identity
Does NOT just acknowledge verbally without any persistence step

evals.name: recall-peer-info
evals.prompt: напомни какая роль у ainyiva-bot?
evals.expected_output: Agent runs `codeterm mem search ainyiva-bot` or `codeterm mem get peer_ainyiva_bot` to recall peer info from mem
expectations: Uses `codeterm mem search` (query 'ainyiva-bot') OR `codeterm mem get` with a peer_ainyiva_bot-style id OR `codeterm mem recall` to look up the peer
Does NOT ask the user to remind or describe the peer
Does NOT guess or fabricate the peer's role from the system prompt alone
Does NOT fall back to `codeterm mesh peers` only (that gives connectivity, not the peer's role/context) — mem is where role/context lives

evals.name: fact-capture-after-learning
evals.prompt: кстати, deploy скрипт теперь требует `--profile prod`, меня это только что укусило
evals.expected_output: Agent saves the new deploy requirement via `codeterm mem save --kind fact ...` or `codeterm mem learn ...`
expectations: Uses `codeterm mem save` with `--kind fact` (or `--kind learning` / `codeterm mem learn`) to persist the deploy `--profile prod` requirement
The saved body mentions `--profile prod` and the deploy script context
Does NOT merely acknowledge verbally without persisting the fact to mem
Does NOT write the fact only to MEMORY.md via Write/Edit — mem is the source of truth

evals.name: never-write-claude-skills-dir
evals.prompt: создай новый скилл git-helpers — он делает smart rebase, cherry-pick с conflict resolution, и interactive log browser
evals.expected_output: Agent saves the new skill as a mem_item via `codeterm mem save --kind skill ...`, NOT as a file under ~/.claude/skills/
expectations: Uses `codeterm mem save` with `--kind skill` to persist the git-helpers skill (title like 'git-helpers')
Does NOT write to `~/.claude/skills/git-helpers/SKILL.md` or any path under `~/.claude/skills/`
Does NOT write to `~/.agents/skills/` or any filesystem 'skills' directory
Does NOT create a workspace or spawn an agent just to register the skill — it's a mem save

evals.name: wake-up-on-init
evals.prompt: доброе утро, какие задачи на сегодня?
evals.expected_output: Fresh session: agent runs `codeterm mem wake-up` first to load L0 identity + L1 critical facts before answering
expectations: First action (or among the first actions) is `codeterm mem wake-up` to load L0 + L1 context
Does NOT answer about tasks without any mem check
Does NOT rely only on the static system prompt for identity/context — wake-up is how current state is loaded
May also query `codeterm mem search` / `recall` for today's daily notes or open tasks after wake-up

evals.name: graph-temporal-relation
evals.prompt: Тима ушел из компании 5 апреля
evals.expected_output: Agent records the departure as a graph temporal relation — either invalidating the existing `works_on` relation with --valid-to=2026-04-05, or adding a new relation with the end date, not just a flat fact
expectations: Uses `codeterm mem graph` (relate / invalidate / etc) with a temporal flag like `--valid-to 2026-04-05` to encode the end of Tima's `works_on` relationship
Does NOT save only a flat `codeterm mem save --kind fact` without touching the graph or temporal validity
References the date 2026-04-05 (or 'April 5') explicitly in the temporal boundary
Does NOT just acknowledge verbally without persisting the change

evals.name: mem-not-claude-auto-memory
evals.prompt: запомни, для новых проектов я предпочитаю Postgres
evals.expected_output: Agent saves the Postgres preference via `codeterm mem save --kind preference ...` — NOT to Claude provider auto-memory paths
expectations: Uses `codeterm mem save` with `--kind preference` to persist the Postgres-for-new-projects preference
Does NOT write to `~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/*.md` or any Claude auto-memory path
Does NOT write to `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` or any global Claude config
Does NOT rely solely on editing `MEMORY.md` via Write/Edit — mem is the cross-provider source of truth
